## Source map — GOV-017

**Source:** INEGI, *ENOE/ENOEN 2022Q4 technical note*; official statistical release. Extract covers pp. 1–23. Release date is not stated; reference period is October–December 2022. No retroactive numerical revisions are reported, but population estimates and historical tabulations were updated from 2014 onward (p. 21).

### Atomic claims

- **Official assertion / estimate:** The working-age population was 99,515,795; PEA 60,145,456 (60.4%), employed 58,349,353, and unemployed 1,796,103 (3.0% of PEA) in 2022Q4 (pp. 1–3, 12).
- **Official comparison:** Versus 2021Q4, PEA increased by 1,383,663, employment by 1,738,142, and unemployment declined by 354,479; these are survey estimates, not administrative counts (p. 3, Table 1).
- **Definition:** Unemployment requires no work during the reference week, willingness to work, and some job-search activity (p. 12). Suboccupation means need and availability to work more hours (p. 10).
- **Official estimate:** Suboccupation was 4.4 million, or 7.5% of employed people, versus 10.6% in 2021Q4; seasonally adjusted suboccupation declined 0.1 percentage points from the prior quarter (p. 10).
- **Definition and estimate:** Broad informal employment includes informal-sector work, unprotected agricultural work, unprotected paid domestic work, and workers lacking social security despite formal units; it totaled 32.157 million, 55.1% of employment, up 548,021 year-on-year (pp. 10–11, Table 5).
- **Contrary/qualification:** Low unemployment coexists with labor-quality concerns: 30.4% were in “critical conditions of employment,” and 55.1% in broad informal employment (pp. 15–16).
- **Methodological change:** From 2022Q3, the pandemic-era classification of certain temporarily absent or wanting-to-work people as “available” ended; prior criteria resumed (pp. 3, 22–23). This limits direct interpretation of some year-to-year PNEA comparisons.
- **Survey design:** Probabilistic, two-stage, stratified cluster sample of private dwellings; five-panel rotation, expansion factors, and quarterly national/state/urban domains (pp. 21–22). Interviews were exclusively face-to-face from 2022Q3 (p. 21).
- **Adjustment/limits:** Seasonal series use X-13ARIMA-SEATS; salary-based indicators require CPI-equivalent wages and are sensitive to minimum-wage changes (pp. 15, 18, 23). The extract reports no confidence intervals or nonresponse rates.
- **Attribution limit:** The release describes labor-market estimates and methodology; it does not establish causation, policy effectiveness, ruler intent, competence, or ruler-attributable outcomes.

**Unresolved allegations:** None.  
**Stronger-model reopen:** pp. 3, 15, 21–23 for comparability, revisions, sampling, and seasonal-adjustment details; tables/annexes for uncertainty estimates.
